LinkedIn post by Hamilton Cabel, posted 1 day ago.

Hooters of America has closed every location it operated in Massachusetts, New York, Connecticut, and Minnesota, part of an ongoing restructuring stemming from the company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing on March 31, 2025. The Northeast franchise group behind the Massachusetts locations had run Hooters restaurants in the region for more than three decades before shutting down.

The company's own language calls this an effort to "focus, revitalize and strengthen" the brand. Four entire states losing every location simultaneously is a specific kind of retrenchment, not a slow decline market by market, but a wholesale retreat from an entire region at once.

A group of original Hooters founders separately agreed to acquire roughly 100 company-owned locations in states including Florida, Texas, Georgia, Indiana, and Illinois as part of the same restructuring, meaning the brand isn't disappearing, it's consolidating hard around its strongest legacy markets and abandoning the ones that never held.
